beats.narration: Checkpoint six: assemble the minimal secure configuration for an agent that fetches untrusted content and writes to one protected path. Four candidate pieces on the table. If you haven't picked yours, pause here first.

The twist in this one: all four pieces belong. The pre-tool-use hook blocks a write outside the permitted path before the tool runs — enforcement, not convention. The deny rule walls off the sensitive paths, limiting the blast radius if the agent is steered. The environment reference keeps the credential out of committed config, where history is forever. And the audit log records every privileged action with its result — the evidence a regulated review asks to see. Put together: the injected write hits the hook block and the audit log, never the disk.
